raw_segments.text: I touched the heath. It was dry and yet warm with the heat of the summer day. I looked
at the sky. It was pure. A kindly star twinkled just above the chasm ridge. The dew fell but
with propitious softness. No breeze whispered. Nature seemed to me benign and good. I thought
she loved me, outcast as I was, and I who from man could anticipate only mistrust, rejection,
insult, clung to her with filial fondness. Tonight, at least, I would be her guest as
I was her child. My mother would lodge me without money and without price. I had one
morsel of bread yet. The remnant of a roll I had bought in a town we passed through at
noon with a stray penny. My last coin. I saw ripe bilberries gleaming here and there, like
jet beads in the heath. I gathered a handful and ate them with the bread. My hunger, sharp
before, was, if not satisfied, appeased by this hermit's meal. I said my evening prayers
at its conclusion, and then chose my couch.
